thread.title: UPDATE: Micron earnings show big profit and sales gains, stock turns green after forecast

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Micron earnings show big profit and sales gains, stock turns green after forecast
text:
By Jeremy C. Owens, MarketWatch
Fourth-quarter projection beat analyst estimates, shows confidence that memory prices will stay high
Micron Technology Inc. continued to post huge gains in profit and revenue amid high memory-chip prices in a Wednesday earnings report, and the company's forecast showed confidence that the rise will continue, pushing shares higher after hours.
Micron (MU) profit more than doubled from the year before, while sales grew by 40%. Micron reported third-quarter net income of $3.82 billion, or $3.10 a share, on sales of $7.8 billion, up from $5.57 billion in the year-ago quarter. After adjustments for stock-based compensation and other effects, the company claimed earnings of $3.15 a share, up from $1.62 a share a year ago.
Analysts on average expected adjusted earnings of $3.13 cents a share on sales of $7.76 billion, according to FactSet, after Micron divulged updated expectations for the quarter late last month in a meeting with analysts. The company had increased its forecast to $3.12 to $3.16 a share on revenue of $7.7 billion to $7.8 billion, up from $2.76 to $2.90 a share on revenue of $7.2 billion to $7.6 billion.
Shares fell about 1% in late trading after numbers were released, but then turned around after Micron Chief Financial Officer Dave Zinsner delivered a fourth-quarter forecast on the conference call that beat analysts' expectations. Micron projected fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.23 to $3.37 a share on revenue of $8 billion to $8.4 billion, beating analysts' average forecast of $3.16 a share on sales of $8.02 billion.
Shares flipped into the green immediately after Zinsner delivered that forecast, moving to gains of as much as 3%. Micron stock has been on a tear as memory prices have increased over the past couple of years, rising 91.4% in the past year as the S&P 500 index has gained 13.4%.
Micron's stock has been juiced by higher prices for its core product, computer memory, which Micron has attributed to demand from cloud-data centers, especially in China. However, the price of memory has attracted the attention of Chinese regulators (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-earnings-china-probe-poses-wild-card-for-highflying-stock-2018-06-15), and analysts and companies -- including tech titan Apple Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-stock-dips-after-apple-cfo-predicts-memory-prices-will-turn-around-this-year-2018-05-01).(AAPL) -- have said of late that they expect the increase in prices to calm soon, potentially in the second half of the year (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-earnings-china-probe-poses-wild-card-for-highflying-stock-2018-06-15).
Micron's forecast suggested it did not expect big price drops, and Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra -- who has repeatedly said that the increased prices are part of a new demand environment (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-ceo-red-hot-memory-market-should-maintain-demand-that-has-elevated-earnings-2017-12-19) that is not as transitory as previous memory cycles -- did not sound concerned Wednesday.
"The industry we operate within is structurally different than in the past," Mehrotra said in Wednesday's conference call. "The results are a more consistent and stable supply/demand outlook."
-Jeremy C. Owens; 415-439-6400; AskNewswires@dowjones.com
